specificationSpec.specificationTitle: Software Loading and Data Transfer Security

specificationContent.para: All software uploads and data transfers to aircraft avionics systems shall follow these security practices per DO-326A / ED-202A cybersecurity requirements:
Data Transfer Device Requirements:
- Use only approved portable maintenance aids (PMAs) or laptops designated for aircraft software loading
- Ensure all data transfer devices are scanned for malware before connecting to aircraft systems
- Maintain virus definition files current (updated within 7 days)
- Use read-only USB devices when possible to prevent inadvertent data writes or malware transfer
Software Package Verification:
- Verify software package integrity and authenticity using manufacturer-provided cryptographic hashes (SHA-256 or stronger) and, where available, digital signatures
- Use non-cryptographic checksums (for example, CRC32) only as supplementary checks for transmission or storage errors, not as a security control
- Confirm software part number matches aircraft configuration database
- Verify digital signature on software package if provided by manufacturer
- Maintain chain of custody documentation from manufacturer to installation
Data Security During Transfer:
- Use encrypted data transfer when loading sensitive configuration data or navigation databases
- Do not load software or data over unsecured wireless connections
- Physically secure data transfer equipment during upload/download operations
- Log all software loading events with timestamp, operator ID, software version, and result
Procedures for downloading and handling flight data from FDR, CVR, QAR, and maintenance systems:
Quick Access Recorder (QAR) Data:
- Download QAR data routinely (daily or after each flight as required by operator)
- Use approved QAR reader device or connect via aircraft Ethernet maintenance port
- Transfer data to secure flight operations quality assurance (FOQA) database
- Encrypt data files during transfer and storage per data protection regulations (GDPR, local laws)
- Limit access to authorized personnel only (flight operations, maintenance, safety departments)
Flight Data Recorder (FDR) Data:
- Download FDR only when required for incident investigation or routine inspection
- Use certified FDR readout equipment from original equipment manufacturer (OEM)
- Maintain strict chain of custody for all FDR data downloads
- Report FDR data downloads to regulatory authority if required by incident/accident investigation
- Never delete or modify FDR data. Original data must be preserved for investigation
Cockpit Voice Recorder (CVR) Data:
- CVR data is protected by aviation privacy regulations. Access is restricted to accident investigators
- Do not download CVR data for routine maintenance purposes
- If download is required for incident investigation, follow regulatory authority procedures
- CVR data must be secured and protected from unauthorized access or disclosure
Ensuring data integrity throughout the data lifecycle:
Pre-Load Validation:
- Verify data format matches LRU requirements (file format, encoding, structure)
- Validate navigation database effective dates and expiration dates
- Check configuration data against aircraft-specific parameters and limitations
- Perform data sanity checks (range checks, format validation) before loading
Post-Load Verification:
- Verify successful data load completion using LRU status indication or test mode
- Compare loaded data checksum against expected value from data package
- Perform functional test of system with new data/software installed
- Document data/software version loaded in aircraft maintenance logbook and configuration database
Data Backup and Retention:
- Maintain backup copies of all loaded software and data packages
- Retain previous software versions for minimum 2 years or per regulatory requirements
- Store backup data in geographically separate location from primary systems
- Test data restore procedures periodically to ensure backup integrity
Maintaining complete traceability of all software and data loaded on aircraft systems:
Configuration Management:
- Maintain master configuration database listing all software part numbers and versions installed
- Update database immediately after any software or data load operation
- Include installation date, installer name, reason for change, and test results
- Cross-reference with aircraft configuration change documents and service bulletins
Version Control:
- Use manufacturer-provided software version numbering scheme
- Document software compatibility matrix (which software versions work together)
- Identify software baseline for aircraft type certificate and supplemental type certificates
- Track deviations from baseline and maintain approval documentation
Audit Trail:
- Create permanent audit log of all software loading operations
- Include failed load attempts and reason for failure
- Maintain log accessible for regulatory audits and safety investigations
- Ensure audit log integrity using tamper-evident or cryptographic methods where required
